<reason>A more convincingly distinguished maintaining restrictive policy during gradual disinflation from abandoning price stability. It answered the credibility challenge with observable progress and conditional intervention, then pressed the relevant comparison: whether faster convergence justifies additional recession damage. B raised a legitimate risk of delayed detection, but repeatedly asserted rather than established that patience guarantees a larger eventual recession. Its concession concerning falling inflation and anchored expectations strengthened A's case, while its characterization of recession costs as bounded remained inadequately defended.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A answered B's attack on the two-quarter trigger by identifying its explicit earlier-action provision and showing that policy-lag uncertainty also undermines promises of a controllable recession. B's closing repeated the mandatory-delay characterization without addressing that correction, leaving its principal objection materially weakened.</best_rebuttal>
